text: . Former Norwegian diplomat Erik Solheim wished Prime Minister Narendra Modi a happy birthday today and highlighted five major changes in India during his government’s tenure.Erik Solheim, former Minister of Climate and the Environment of Norway, reflected on Prime Minister Modi’s political tenure and outlined five areas that, in his view, have undergone significant changes. He identified “Direction” as the first major change, saying PM Modi had given India a new purpose through his leadership and emphasis on the vision of ‘Viksit Bharat’ or a developed India by 2047. On infrastructure, Solheim said that the Modi government had overseen a major expansion in roads, railways, airports and ports.Solheim also highlighted the environment as another area of change. He said India had moved from being behind Europe on environmental issues to becoming the world’s second-largest solar market and third-largest renewable economy. He cited India’s leadership of the G20 and BRICS and said the country had become more visible and influential internationally.The fifth area identified by Solheim was “Pride”. He said PM Modi had contributed to a renewed sense of pride in India by emphasising Indian traditions, history and cultural heritage.Several foreign diplomats and missions in New Delhi extended warm wishes to Prime Minister Narendra Modi on his 76th birthday, while reflecting the close bond and enduring partnership India shares with countries worldwide under his leadership. The US Embassy in India conveyed heartfelt birthday greetings to PM Modi on behalf of US President Donald Trump.Japan’s Ambassador to India, Ono Keiichi, hailed Prime Minister Modi’s leadership in advancing the vision of a ‘Viksit Bharat’, while expressing hope that the India-Japan partnership would reach greater heights as the two countries prepare to mark 75 years of diplomatic relations next year.Australian High Commissioner to India, Philip Green, recalled the warmth surrounding PM Modi’s recent visit to the island nation and the strong people-to-people ties between the two countries.Extending warm birthday greetings to PM Modi, Slovak Ambassador Robert Maxian also recalled the “warmth, friendship and memorable moments” during the Indian leader’s recent visit to Slovakia.

. The government has introduced an exemption from the requirement of Registration-cum-Membership Certificate RCMC or Certificate of Registration for small-value export consignments up to three lakh rupees. The Ministry of Commerce and Industry said that the measure is aimed at reducing the compliance burden for new and small exporters and facilitating exports through Postal, Courier and other emerging channels. The Ministry added that export consignments exceeding three lakh rupees will continue to require a valid RCMC or Certificate of Registration, wherever applicable.The Ministry said that the measure provides MSMEs, artisans, small businesses and first-time exporters with a simpler entry point into international markets by removing the requirement to obtain an RCMC. It added that the move will enable emerging exporters to test overseas markets and establish an export track record with lower initial compliance requirements.The exemption will also facilitate e-commerce and other emerging export channels. The move is also aimed at supporting low-value exports through Postal, Courier and other emerging channels that are increasingly enabling businesses to reach international customers.The Ministry further said that as exporters expand their operations and their consignments move beyond the three lakh rupees threshold, they can obtain membership of the relevant Export Promotion Councils or Commodity Boards and access export promotion, market access and other institutional support services.

. The Ministry of Education, in coordination with the External Affairs Ministry is organizing a two day Bharat Innovates Exposition from today at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi to showcase India’s Deep-Tech innovations as a lead up to and alongside the 18th BRICS Summit 2026. The Exposition is showcasing 37 India’s Deep-Tech startups and ventures alligning with the theme of India’s BRICS Chairship Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability. The event is providing participating innovators an opportunity to network with CEOs, investors, business leaders and industry representatives from BRICS member countries. Ministry of Eduaction said that the event will facilitate opportunities for Business to Business engagements, technology partnerships, investment discussions, business linkages and international market access.

. The North East Zone Inter-State Badminton Championship 2026 has returned to Meghalaya for the first time since 2016. The tournament serves as the official qualifying ground for the team events of the highly anticipated National Games 2027 in the state.Underway at the Jawaharlal Nehru Indoor Sports Complex, Shillong, the championship will continue till 19th September 2026. More than 250 top-tier shuttlers representing all eight Northeastern states – Assam, Arunachal Pradesh, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Manipur, Nagaland, Tripura, and Sikkim have come together for the championship.Wailadmiki Shylla, Minister of Sports and Youth Affairs, Government of Meghalaya said that the return of this important championship to Shillong after ten long years arrives at a highly opportune moment, as Meghalaya prepares to host the 39th National Games next year. He added that the State witnessed a surge in the Sports budget from a mere ₹40 crore eight to nine years ago to a staggering ₹844 crore.The objective of the funding is to provide better infrastructure, platforms, and opportunities for the youth, alongside a hike in prize money that now awards ₹2 lakh to National Games gold medallists. Furthermore, Shylla underscored the transformative Meghalaya Outstanding Direct Appointment Policy, which guarantees direct government jobs to State athletes who secure medals at major events.The policy also allows athletes a grace period of up to ten years to pursue higher education or advance their sporting careers before taking up their appointed posts. Turning to National Games preparations, he confirmed that a dedicated stipend will be provided to the final selected team to support their ongoing training.Ace shuttler Ashmita Chaliha, the first Indian ever to win the Korea Masters Title, who is representing Assam in the tournament, commended the sports momentum as she returned to compete in Shillong at the North East Inter-State Badminton Championship after nearly a decade. Expressing optimism regarding the host State’s venue readiness and infrastructure build-up for the upcoming National Games next year, Chaliha highlighted the rise of grassroots talent across the region. She observed that while young shuttlers are emerging through structured training, grooming and high-level match exposure will be essential to bridge the gap with elite circuits. Offering a message to Meghalaya’s athletes, she urged them to play without the burden of expectations.Beyond the competition, the successful hosting of the championship underscores a larger milestone for Meghalaya. As the State prepares to host the 39th National Games next year, hosting a premier regional event of this scale functions as a practical demonstration of Shillong’s operational readiness.

. Russian President Vladimir Putin today extended wishes to Prime Minister Narendra Modi on his 76th birthday and lauded his contribution towards strengthening the Special and Privileged Strategic Partnership between the two nations.The Russian Embassy in India shared President Putin’s message for PM Modi on Instagram. In the message, President Putin expressed gratitude for the warm welcome and hospitality extended during his recent visit to New Delhi for the 18th BRICS Summit.According to the statement, President Putin described his recent talks with Prime Minister Modi as “substantive, frank and productive” and said he is ready to continue cooperation between the two nations on bilateral and international issues.

. India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast heavy rainfall over Bihar, East Madhya Pradesh, East Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, West Bengal and North Eastern parts of the country during the next two days. IMD said that thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds are likely to prevail over Andhra Pradesh, Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Bihar, Jharkhand, Karnataka, Odisha, Sub-Himalayan West Bengal and Sikkim tomorrow. Meanwhile, Coastal Andhra Pradesh, Kerala and Mahe are expected to experience hot and humid weather till 8th of this month.

. The ‘Aashirwad Ka Diya’ programme was held across Andhra Pradesh last evening as part of the Seva Sankalp Abhiyan, organised to mark Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s 25 years in public life. People and public representatives in several parts of the state lit lamps at their homes and iconic places as part of the programme.Union Minister Pemmasani Chandrasekhar participated in the programme at Guntur, and Union Minister Bhupathiraju Srinivasa Varma took part in the programme at Bhimavaram in West Godavari district. BJP State President P. V. N. Madhav participated in the programme at Tirupati, while Minister Satya Kumar Yadav took part in the programme at Vijayawada. Minister Nara Lokesh also lit an earthen lamp at his residence in Amaravati as part of the programme.

. India remains firmly committed to ensuring energy security for its 1.4 billion people and will continue to do so through diversified sourcing and on the basis of evolving market dynamics. Noting the passage of the Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act in the US Congress, the External Affairs Ministry stated that it is monitoring further developments on this matter.According to the ministry, this issue has been discussed at high levels in recent months with various US interlocutors. Its potential implications for not just the bilateral relationship but also the international energy market have been very clearly articulated by the Indian side.The Ministry further said that the Indian side has also made clear its determination to take all necessary measures to protect its trade and economic interests. Government will work closely with Indian trade and industry bodies to deal with the implications of these developments.
. In the Indian bullion market today, 24 carat gold was one per cent up at 1,52,362 rupees per 10 grams. Silver rose 1.1 per cent to 2,31,337 rupees per kilogram.

. India’s retail inflation accelerated to 4.82 per cent in August on an annual basis, remaining above the Reserve Bank of India’s target of four per cent for the third consecutive month this year. The August inflation reading was higher than the 4.45 per cent recorded in July as food prices remained elevated.According to data released by the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation, inflation in rural areas increased to 5.23 per cent, while in urban regions it rose to 4.31 per cent. The food inflation rate, based on the All India Consumer Food Price Index, stood at 5.95 per cent last month, up from 5.52 per cent in the preceding month.According to the data, the increase in inflation during the last month was mainly attributed to rising prices in personal care, social protection, restaurants and accommodation services, food, beverages and intoxicants. The top items showing high inflation at the all-India combined level included Silver, Gold, Diamond and Platinum Jewellery, Ginger, Onion and Garlic. In contrast, items with lowest inflation included Tomato, Potato, Car, Lady’s finger, Parwal and Kundru.

. Benchmark domestic equity indices today ended almost flat. The Sensex dipped 22 points to close at 74,315. The Nifty added 53 points to settle at 23,271.In the broader market on the National Stock Exchange, the Midcap 100 index gained 0.9 per cent, while the Smallcap 100 index added 0.8 per cent.Earlier, the markets opened mildly lower after a hawkish stance from the US Federal Reserve and concerns over geopolitical developments. However, both the indices soon recovered and traded with gains for most of the volatile session, supported by value buying.In the Sensex pack, 21 out of 30 companies logged gains. Among the top performers, Tata Steel climbed 2.8 per cent, Bharat Electronics Limited surged 2.4 per cent and Indigo gained 2.3 per cent. In contrast, HDFC Bank declined 1.3 per cent, Titan dipped over 1.1 per cent and ICICI Bank fell one per cent.In the sectoral indices on the BSE, 18 out of 28 sectors edged upward. Among the top gainers, Insurance advanced 3.2 per cent, Capital Goods jumped nearly two per cent, and Industrials gained one and a half per cent.  In contrast, Top 10 Banks declined 0.7 per cent, Private Banks Index shed 0.6 per cent and Bankex dropped half a per cent.The overall market breadth at the BSE was positive, as shares of 2 thousand 686 companies advanced, 1 thousand 642 declined and 207 remained unchanged.

. India has rejected the so-called Pakistan-China Boundary Joint Commission, saying Pakistan has no locus standi to enter into arrangements concerning Indian territory under its illegal and forcible occupation.Spokesperson of the Ministry of External Affairs Randhir Jaiswal said this while responding to media queries yesterday. He said the Ministry has seen reports in this regard and India’s position is clear and consistent. He said there is no boundary between Pakistan. Mr Jaiswal said, New Delhi rejects the Pakistan-China Boundary Joint Commission, which is without any legal basis.The spokesperson reiterated that the Union Territories of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh have been, are, and will always remain integral and inalienable parts of India. He said India has never recognised the so-called 1963 China-Pakistan Boundary Agreement and has consistently maintained that it is illegal and invalid.The MEA spokesperson said, New Delhi resolutely opposes and rejects any attempt to alter the status of the occupied territories or legitimise what it calls illegal occupation. New Delhi called upon Pakistan to immediately vacate areas under its illegal and forcible occupation instead of engaging in such theatrics.

. In Chess, Indian Women’s Team began their campaign with a commanding 4-0 victory over the Dominican Republic at the 46th World Chess Olympiad in Samarkand, Uzbekistan, yesterday.Top-ranked Indian Koneru Humpy made a winning start with a victory over Franchesca Ramirez Luzon, while R Vaishali had a smooth outing against Miguelina De La Rosa Martinez. Vantika Agrawal had to work harder for her victory over Mary Loly Gonzalez Peguero. B Savitha Shri also celebrated her Olympic debut with a win over Karla Mya Nunez Diaz.Indian Men’s team also began its campaign with a victory, with world champion D Gukesh, Nihal Sarin and Vidit Gujrathi registering a convincing 3-1 victory over Thailand. Nihal was the first Indian to win, defeating Thanadon Kulpruethanon, before Gukesh produced a brilliant attacking display to beat Faris Rashid Alriyami. Vidit then completed a comfortable victory over Tupfah Khumnorkaew. However, Arjun Erigaisi went down to Prin Laohawirapap after being in a position of strength for much of the game.The Olympiad, one of the biggest events in the chess calendar, has attracted teams from across the world. Each team can have five players in its squad, with four featuring in each round.

. Vultures are extremely important for our ecosystem. By feeding on dead animals, they help keep the environment clean and reduce the spread of harmful diseases.However, vulture populations have declined significantly because of habitat loss, poisoning, and certain veterinary medicines that are harmful to them. Conservation efforts are therefore essential to protect these birds and maintain the balance of nature.On this International Vulture Day, government and environmental experts have urged people to understand, protect, and conserve vultures for a healthier environment.

. The Supreme Court today asked the Central Board of Secondary Education , CBSE to consider deferring its mandatory three-language policy for Class 6 students to the 2027 academic session to ease the transition for students. A bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi, and Justice V. Mohana suggested the delay to comfort students, adding that those currently in Class 6 who wish to study three languages this year should still be allowed to do so.The policy, aligned with the National Education Policy 2020, requires students to study three languages, at least two of which must be native Indian languages. Under the CBSE circular, foreign languages can only be taken as a third or fourth subject.

. The first meeting of the Joint Parliamentary Committee on the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026, will be held in New Delhi today. The Committee will receive a briefing from representatives of the Ministry of Home Affairs on the provisions of the Bill.Both Houses of Parliament, on 12th August, gave their nod to referring the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026, to a Joint Parliamentary Committee for further scrutiny. The Bill seeks to amend the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act, 2010, with the objective of making the use of foreign contributions more transparent and accountable.The Committee comprises 21 members from the Lok Sabha, nominated by the Speaker, and 10 members from the Rajya Sabha, nominated by the Chairman. Lok Sabha MP Sanjay Jaiswal will head the Joint Panel. Prominent members from the Lok Sabha include Tejaswi Surya, Nishikant Dubey, A. Raja and Supriya Sule. From the Rajya Sabha, Harsh Vardhan Shringla, Sanjay Kumar Jha, Praful Patel and Menaka Guruswamy are among the members of the Committee. The Committee is required to submit its report to the House by the last day of the first week of the Winter Session.

. In Hockey, India’s men’s and women’s teams have clinched the Junior Asia Cup titles at Moqi in China today. The Indian Men’s team defeated South Korea four-one in the final to successfully defend its title. Ajeet Yadav, Anmol Ekka, Prabhdeep Singh and Ashu Maurya scored for India. With this victory, India became the first team in the history of the tournament to win the Men’s title four times, following earlier triumphs in 2015, 2023 and 2024.The Indian women’s team also emerged victorious, defeating hosts China one-nil in the final. Sanika Chandrakant Mane scored the only goal in the 17th minute to secure the title for India. The victory completed a hat-trick of Junior Asia Cup titles for the Indian women’s team, which had previously won in 2023 and 2024.Both the Indian men’s and women’s teams have also qualified for the Junior Hockey World Cup by winning their respective Asia Cup titles.Prime Minister Narendra Modi has congratulated India’s Junior Women’s Hockey Team on retaining the Asia Cup title with an unbeaten campaign. In a social media post, Mr. Modi said the team’s success reflects the talent and determination of the players and extended his best wishes to the entire team.The Prime Minister also congratulated the Junior Men’s Hockey Team on winning the Asia Cup with an emphatic 4-1 victory over South Korea in the final. Describing the achievement as remarkable, Mr. Modi said it reflects the immense talent of the young players.Home Minister Amit Shah has congratulated junior women’s hockey team on winning the Asia Cup and bringing pride and joy to the entire nation. Sharing a social media post, Mr Shah said that their victory and dominant display of sporting prowess will inspire more budding players to join the list of India’s champions. Mr Shah also congratulated Indian junior men’s hockey team for winning the Asia Cup. He added that with the vigour and command of the game, they have once again demonstrated that true mettle of Indian sportsmanship and set an inspiring example for others to follow.

. Today is World Suicide Prevention Day. The day is observed worldwide to raise awareness about suicide prevention and the importance of mental health.The occasion reminds us that people facing emotional distress or difficult circumstances need timely support, understanding and appropriate care. Experts emphasise that listening to someone with patience and without judgement can encourage them to seek help and support.On this Day, people are encouraged to remain attentive to the emotional well-being of those around them and, when required, guide them towards family members, trusted persons or mental health professionals.

. The Election Commission of India has barred both factions of the Trinamool Congress from using the party’s name and election symbol in the upcoming Assembly bypolls in Nandigram and Rejinagar in West Bengal. In an interim order issued yesterday, the Commission said neither the Mamata Banerjee-led group nor the Arup Roy-led group can use the name All India Trinamool Congress or the party’s reserved twin-flower symbol.Both groups will have to contest the bypolls under different names and with election symbols allotted by the Commission. This arrangement will continue until the dispute is finally settled. The Commission said documents and claims submitted by both sides show that there are currently two rival groups within the Trinamool Congress, with both claiming to be the real party. As the dispute cannot be settled before the upcoming bypolls, the Commission has taken this temporary step to decide who can use the party’s name and symbol for now.

. In Men’s Cricket, India defeated Afghanistan by 7 wickets in the first T20 International at the Arun Jaitley Stadium in Delhi last night, taking a 1-0 lead in the three-match series.After India won the toss and chose to bowl first, Afghanistan struggled early and collapsed to 43 for 5. A strong 83-run partnership between Azmatullah Omarzai and Mohammad Nabi pushed Afghanistan’s final score to 156 for 8 in 20 overs. For India, Arshdeep Singh picked up 3 wickets for 19 runs.India chased down the target comfortably, reaching 157 for 3 in just 13.4 overs with 38 balls left. Opener Abhishek Sharma was named Player of the Match for a blistering 82 runs off 32 balls, sharing a massive 121-run stand with Ishan Kishan.The remaining two matches of the series will be played at the same venue on Tuesday and Thursday.

. On the eve of Raksha Bandhan, President Droupadi Murmu has extended greetings to people. The President said that the festival of Raksha Bandhan has been an integral part of country’s culture and tradition since ancient times. She said that rakhi thread, tied around the wrist with faith, is regarded as a sacred bond of protection, known as Raksha Bandhan.The President  said that in many shlokas and mantras, Rakshe, Ma Chala, Ma Chala can be found which expresses the imploration that may this bond of protection continue forever. President Murmu urged every citizen to take a pledge to strengthen the bonds amongst families and communities, marching forward with this spirit towards a Viksit Bharat.Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla also extended greetings to countrymen on the eve of Raksha Bandhan. In his message, Mr Birla said festival that celebrates the mutual love, affection, and trust between brothers and sisters. He noted that the festival symbolizes of India’s rich culture, family values, and the unbreakable bonds of affection and belonging.

. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast heavy rainfall in Bihar, Odisha, Sub-Himalayan West Bengal, Sikkim, Kerala and Rajasthan today. The Met Department has predicted thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds in Uttarakhand, Andhra Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Konkan, Goa, Karnataka and Lakshadweep today. Similar weather conditions are expected over Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, Karaikal, Kerala, Mahe, parts of Northeast India and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands during the next two days. The weather agency has forecast a partly cloudy sky in the national capital today.

. Global crude oil prices declined today. Brent crude was trading 1.2 per cent down at 107 US dollars and 44 cents per barrel in intra-day trade at a time of writing this report. Meanwhile, West Texas Intermediate crude was trading 1.8 per cent lower at 103 US dollars and 93 cents per barrel.

. Top-ranked India’s Dhiraj Bommadevara scripted history by becoming the first Indian male recurve archer to win gold at the World Cup Final, edging Japan’s Nakanishi Junya in a thrilling shoot-off at Saltillo in Mexico.The 25-year-old World Number 10 Army man produced a dominant run, powering through the quarterfinals and semifinals before overcoming world No. 20 Nakanishi 6-5 in a hard-fought five-setter. After a 5-5 tie, Dhiraj prevailed 10-9 in the shoot-off. He also ended a 16-year wait for an Indian male recurve archer to win a medal in this prestigious event. Jayanta Talukdar was the last male recurve archer to win a medal – a bronze in Edinburgh 2010.Dola Banerjee remains the only other Indian to have won World Cup Final gold, claiming the women’s individual title in the 2007 edition in Dubai.

. The Federal Reserve in United States raised its benchmark interest rate for the first time since 2023 in an effort to lower persistent high inflation. The central bank also signalled that another rate hike could occur later this year. The quarter-point increase lifts the Fed’s key rate to about 3.9 percent and, over time, could result in higher borrowing costs for mortgages, auto loans, and credit cards. In a set of quarterly projections, the Fed also signalled that its rate-setting committee expects to hike rates a second time to 4.1 per cent.The move comes as Americans are already struggling with high costs for groceries, gas, and housing. Affordability has taken on a leading role in the upcoming midterm elections, just seven weeks away.In a press conference following the Fed’s announcement, Chair of Federal Reserve, Kevin Warsh emphasised that the economy has shown signs of gathering speed since the central bank decided to keep rates unchanged in late July. Inflation has also remained stubbornly above the Fed’s 2 per cent target and he noted that there is little sign it is cooling. Warsh also said renewed combat between the US and Iran, which has driven up gas prices, also convinced Fed officials to support rate hikes.According to the Fed’s preferred measure, inflation was 3.7 per cent in July this year compared with a year ago, up from 2.3 per cent in April last year, just before Trump unveiled sweeping tariffs.US President Donald Trump has called for sharply lower interest rates following Fed’s decision. In a post on Truth Social, Trump asserted that US interest rates should be 1 per cent, or less, maintaining that the nation warrants cheaper credit. Trump also associated his demands for monetary relaxation with the national trade balance, asserting that the country could accumulate a minimum of 1.5 trillion dollars annually by halting commerce with states generating a trade deficit.

. Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman today met her Nepalese counterpart Dr Swarnim Wagle in New Delhi. During the meeting, the two Ministers discussed the impact of the floods and Nepal’s priorities for reconstruction and rehabilitation. Dr. Wagle thanked the Finance Minister for India’s support and expressed appreciation for the assistance extended by India, including relief supplies and technical support for rescue and relief efforts. Both sides also emphasised the importance of further strengthening the trade and economic partnership between India and Nepal. The discussions covered strengthening of bilateral economic ties in various areas, as well as initiatives to enhance connectivity for deepening of trade, investments and people-to-people exchanges.

. The National Testing Agency (NTA) has released the final answer keys for the UGC-NET June 2026 examination conducted in three subjects: English, Commerce and Sociology. The keys have been made available on the official website https://ugcnet.nta.nic.in/. The examination was held on September 9th and 10th of this month at 454 centres across 272 cities in the country.The agency had earlier issued a notice on August 16, 2026, regarding the conduct of the test. Candidates who appeared in the examination can now log in to the registration portal using their application number and password to view the final answer keys of their respective subjects. The NTA has advised all candidates to visit the official UGC-NET website regularly for the latest updates related to the examination. For any clarification, candidates may contact the NTA Help Desk through the contact details provided on the website.

. Union Minister for Rural Development, Agriculture and Farmers Welfare Shivraj Singh Chouhan has directed officials to explore how the Viksit Bharat-GRAM G Scheme can contribute to building Viksit Gaon. Addressing a national workshop, organised on the Viksit Bharat-G RAM G.  Mr Chouhan stressed that along with providing employment, the scheme should facilitate the creation of assets that remain useful to rural communities over the long term and help make villages self-reliant and developed. The Minister directed officials to conduct random inspections of works being undertaken under the scheme. He said that work should not merely mean digging soil at one place and dumping it at another. He stressed that, keeping in view the objective of “Viksit Gaon for a Viksit Bharat”, works under the scheme should create a strong foundation for village development and strengthen the rural economy.Mr Chouhan also emphasised adherence to the wage-material ratio under the scheme. He said that at the district level, 60 per cent of the funds are to be spent on wages and 40 per cent on material. The Minister also planted saplings in New Delhi on the occasion of Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s birthday. The workshop was attended by elected representatives of Panchayati Raj Institutions, Commissioners and senior officials of States and Union Territories, and other participants.

. BJP’s month-long nationwide Seva Sankalp Abhiyaan has begun from today to mark the completion of 25 years of Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s public life and service. As part of the Seva Sankalp Abhiyaan which will continue till 17th of next month, the first day of the campaign is being observed as Seva Diwas, under which blood donation camps have been organised across the country.Party President Nitin Nabin inaugurated blood donation camp at the Party Headquarters in New Delhi. Mr Nabin along with other party leaders and workers also donated blood. Later talking to media on the occasion, BJP chief said, party workers across the country are participating in these blood donation camp. He noted that under the leadership of the Prime Minister Modi lives of the citizens have been transformed. Mr Nabin said under the leadership of Prime Minister Modi, India is rapidly moving on the path of development to achieve the goal of Viksit Bharat by 2047.In Delhi, Chief Minister Rekha Gupta performed hawan at Khatu Shyam temple. Later talking to media, Ms Gupta said that she wished for Prime Minister’s long life and good health. She added that, inspired by Mr Modi’s constant emphasis on public service, Delhi government has organised various government-led programs today.

. The Archaeological Survey of India has notified Gollala Gudi Temple at Palampet in the Mulugu district of Telangana as a monument of national importance. The Ministry of culture said that the temple is situated near the UNESCO listed Ramappa Temple and is renowned for its exquisite carvings and architectural heritage.The temple is a Trikutalaya and consists of a mandapa facing East and surrounded by three garbhagriha.A monument of national importance in the country is protected under the Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains Act, 1958. The Archaeological Survey of India takes charge of such sites for conservation, maintenance, and regulated public access

. The Government has announced the Tenzing Norgay National Adventure Awards for the year 2024. The awards recognise outstanding achievements by individuals in the field of adventure and seek to promote a spirit of endurance, risk-taking, teamwork and quick and effective decision-making in challenging situations. The awards are given in four categories, which are Land Adventure, Water Adventure, Air Adventure and Lifetime Achievement. Each awardee will receive a statuette, a certificate and award money of 15 lakh rupees. The awardees are Baljeet Kaur and Skalzang Rigzin in Land Adventure category, Rimo Saha in Water Adventure category and Shiv Prasad Chamoli in the Life Time Achievement category.The selections were made following the recommendations of the National Selection Committee. The Committee evaluated the nominations and recommended the awardees for conferment of the national honour.The awards seek to promote among the youth a spirit of courage, endurance, discipline, risk-taking and cooperative teamwork, while encouraging the ability to respond with speed and effectiveness in challenging situations. President Droupadi Murmu will confer the awards along with the National Sports Awards 2025. The date of the award ceremony will be announced later.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi today stated that India is taking every step needed to become a preferred destination for the semiconductor industry. Inaugurating SEMICON India 2026 at Yashobhoomi in New Delhi today, Mr Modi said the world is looking for new and trusted manufacturing destinations and India is steadily preparing itself to meet this need. Mr Modi highlighted that India’s semiconductor ecosystem is expanding rapidly and opening new opportunities for innovation, investment and growth.. He discussed how the explosive demand for Artificial Intelligence is shifting the focus from mere transistor size to holistic system integration, including memory placement and heat management.Mr Modi said that on one side India’s economy is growing and the other side, global trust in India is also growing. He said, despite the challenging global environment, India recorded a growth rate of 7.8 per cent. Prime Minister said, at the same time, Japan’s credit rating agency also upgraded India’s sovereign rating. Mr Modi said, every citizen of the country is working with a commitment to build a developed India. Prime Minister said, India’s semiconductor ecosystem is expanding rapidly and it is is opening new opportunities for innovation, investment and growth.Prime Minister Modi said, India Semiconductor Mission 2.0 expanded outlay to 13.5 billion US dollar from eight billion US dollar in the first phase. He highlighted that so far 12 chip making projects have been approved in the next phase it will further increase.In his address, the Prime Minister also mentioned about recently held BRICS Summit in New Delhi. He said, India successfully hosted the summit in which New Delhi Declaration was adopted with consensus of every member country. Mr Modi said, it is another major testament to the world’s trust in India.He said, young talents who are researching in India should come forward. Mr Modi said, the youth who are researching abroad should also join the development of advanced technologies in India. He urged industry leaders to spearhead Research and Development in the country. He added that this will be mutually beneficial, driving industry growth while empowering India’s youth.On the occasion, Union Minister of Electronics and IT Ashwini Vaishnaw said that India had wanted to establish a semiconductor industry for several decades, but it was possible only under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi. He said, the foundation has now been laid and the next step is to build the industry through Semicon 2.0, which  focuses on six major pillars. This include semiconductor design, machines and materials, memory, silicon, compound and logic fabrication units and research and development. He said, the  government has set a target to support at least 200 startups and companies to design chips in India across the spectrum of semiconductor requirements.Minister of State for Electronics and IT Jitin Prasada, Secretary S Krishnan, officials, delegations were present on the occasion.The SEMICON India 2026 event has brought together over 600 exhibitors, 300 international companies, and delegations from more than 50 countries. The exhibition features six country pavilions representing Japan, South Korea, Malaysia, Netherlands, Singapore and Sweden, twelve State Government pavilions, and a dedicated Startup Pavilion.The conference and exhibition, being held from today is being organised on the theme Silicon to Systems: Building the Ecosystem. It has brought together global and Indian companies, policymakers, investors, researchers, start-ups, academic institutions and students from across the semiconductor and electronics value chain.

. The Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) has revised hallmarking charges for gold and silver articles. The hallmarking fee for gold has been increased from 45 to 75 rupees per article, while the charge for silver remains unchanged at 35 rupees per article. The revised charges will come into effect immediately, ahead of the festive season.The increase in gold hallmarking charges has been notified through the BIS (Hallmarking) Amendment Regulations, 2026, dated 14th of this month.Under the amended Schedule IV, jewellers will have to pay a hallmarking fee of 75 rupees per gold article, subject to a minimum charge of 200 rupees per consignment. For silver articles, the fee payable by jewellers to recognised Assaying and Hallmarking Centres (AHCs) remains 35 rupees per article, with a minimum charge of 150 rupees per consignment.BIS hallmarking verifies the purity of precious metals used in jewellery and certifies the article under the Bureau of Indian Standards. A hallmarked article carries three key markings: the BIS logo, the Karat fineness, and a six-digit alphanumeric Hallmark Unique Identification (HUID) number.

. The government today said that it will take all necessary steps to protect its economic interests and ensure energy security. The External Affairs Ministry said that country remains firmly committed to ensuring energy security for its 140 crore people and will continue to do so through diversified sourcing and on the basis of evolving market dynamics. The statement came amid the passing of a bill by the US House of Representative that will allow US President Donald Trump to impose tariffs of up to 100 per cent on countries such as India and China for procuring Russian crude oil.The Ministry said that this issue has been discussed at high levels in recent months with various US interlocutors. Its potential implications for not just the bilateral relationship but also the international energy market have been very clearly articulated by the Indian side. The Ministry said that the Indian side has also made clear its determination to take all necessary measures to protect its trade and economic interests. The government made it clear that it will work closely with Indian trade and industry bodies to deal with the implications of these developments.The sanctions bill was passed by the US Senate last month. The House of Representatives passed the bill in a 262-159 vote last evening. It will become a law once US President signs it. The bill seeks to impose sanctions not only on Russia’s leadership and energy sector, but also on the shadow fleet of vessels that enable Moscow to evade sanctions on oil deliveries. It also seeks to authorise US President to impose stiff tariffs on China, India and other countries to reduce their dependence on Russian oil and gas, as well as additional sanctions on Iran.

. In Men’s Cricket, India defeated Afghanistan by seven wickets in the second T20 International at the Arun Jaitley Stadium in Delhi last night, to take an unassailable 2-nil lead in the three-match series.Chasing a target of 160 runs, India comfortably reached 163 for 3 in 14.5 overs. Sanju Samson top-scored with a blistering 57 off 22 balls, while Abhishek Sharma contributed 39 runs off 19 balls. Ishan Kishan remained unbeaten on 38 off 23 balls to guide India home.Earlier, put into bat, Afghanistan posted 159 for 8 in their stipulated 20 overs. Captain Ibrahim Zadran was their top scorer, making 37 runs off 33 balls. For India, Nitish Kumar Reddy claimed three wickets, while Arshdeep Singh took two wickets.Reddy was adjudged Player of the Match. India had won the toss and elected to field. The third and final match of the series will be played at the same venue in Delhi tomorrow.

. In Asian markets today, South Korea’s Kospi declined 0.8 per cent, while Japan’s Nikkei 225 remained largely unchanged.In European markets, London’s FTSE 100 dropped 0.2 per cent, while Germany’s DAX was trading on a flat note, when reports last came in.

. Science and Technology Minister Dr Jitendra Singh has said that critical minerals are key to India’s energy security, industrial competitiveness and national security. The Minister said this while addressing a special plenary of the 3rd Global Summit on Advanced Materials, Critical Minerals, and Metals in New Delhi. Dr Singh said that critical minerals and metals will be a driving component of the next phase of technological development, with their importance extending beyond mining to energy security, industrial competitiveness and national security. He said that the global economy is undergoing a paradigm shift, with clean energy, electric mobility, semiconductors, telecommunications, aerospace, defence and nuclear energy emerging as major drivers of technological and industrial transformation. He added, India is now participating in this global discourse with much greater confidence and is preparing to assume a larger global role.Dr. Singh has called for early industry linkage with research and innovation, saying potential industry partners should be brought on board right from the beginning. He further said that a healthy synergy among research, industry, government and the non-government sector is essential for sustaining startups and entrepreneurs. The Minister also highlighted on building domestic capabilities for energy security as the world moves towards cleaner and greener sources of energy. He said that India’s next phase of growth in strategic technologies and materials will depend on working together of all stakeholders.

. The government has extended the last date for submission of applications by selected meritorious students for National Means cum Merit Scholarship Scheme (NMMSS) for 2026-27 to 30th September this year. The NMMSS is implemented through the National Scholarship Portal (NSP). Following the extension, the last date for Level-1 verification at the Institute Nodal Officer is 15th October while the last date for Level-2 verification with the District Nodal Officer is 31st October.The National Means-cum-Merit Scholarship Scheme awards scholarships to meritorious students from economically weaker sections to prevent drop-out of students after elementary level that is Class eight and encourage them to complete their school education up to higher secondary level that is Class 12. The scholarship amount is 12 thousand rupees per annum per student.The Scheme provides one lakh fresh scholarships every year for Class 9 students who clear the qualifying exam for the scholarship conducted by the State and UT governments. The scholarship is continued through renewal mode from Classes 10 to 12 based on the student’s academic performance. The scheme is applicable only to students studying in State Government, Government-aided and local body schools.The eligibility parameters for availing the scholarship include parental income of not more than 3.50 lakh rupees per annum, a minimum of 55 per cent marks or equivalent grade in the Class 8 examination for appearing in the selection test for award of scholarship. The government has advised all the eligible students to complete their scholarship applications on the National Scholarship Portal within the extended timeline.

. At least 19 people were injured after a Russian barrage of missiles and drones targeted Ukraine’s capital and surrounding region overnight this morning. The attacks hit more than 10 locations in Kyiv and damaged 33 sites across the wider region. Further south in Odesa, seven people were injured and a Russian drone struck a Tanzanian-flagged merchant ship, killing its captain and injuring three crew members.Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Ukrainian forces launched retaliatory strikes against a military airfield in Rostov and an oil refinery in Yaroslavl. Meanwhile, Moscow claimed its military hit Ukrainian energy, industrial, and transport infrastructure, including vessels at the port of Chornomorsk.The escalation comes as peace efforts remain stalled over territorial concessions and security guarantees. Zelenskyy said Ukraine would only halt its strikes if Russia ceases attacks on Ukrainian energy sites. In a separate development, Ukrainian officials today said they had received the bodies of 252 fallen soldiers as part of an ongoing exchange of war dead with Russia.

. India’s textile exports increased to over 29,700 crore rupees in August this year as compared to over 25,600 crore rupees during same month of the last year. The Ministry of Textiles said that the exports increased by 16.1 per cent as compared to August 2025. It added that during April-August 2026, cumulative textile exports reached over 1,40,000 crore rupees, registering growth of 10.3 per cent over the corresponding period of the previous year.The Ministry said that the sustained growth across major segments reflects the increasing competitiveness and diversification of India’s textile export basket. It added that the growth is supported by improved market access, policy interventions and continued efforts towards value addition and market diversification.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has shared an article written by athlete PV Sindhu in which she described how India never lacked talent but often missed opportunities and pathways to realise big dreams.Sharing a social media post, the Prime Minister noted that the article reflects on how the last 12 years have changed this, enabling a new generation of Indians not just to dream big, but to turn those dreams into reality.

. Union Minister of State for Youth Affairs and Sports Raksha Nikhil Khadse said progress in sports is an important aspect of nation-building as India works towards its goal of becoming a developed nation by 2047.The Union Minister, who arrived in Mizoram on a three-day visit visited the Sports Authority of India centre at Mission Veng. There, she met Mizoram Sports Minister Lalnghinglova Hmar, officials of the Sports Department and representatives of various sports organisations, who apprised her of their needs and concerns.Speaking exclusively to Akashvani News, Khadse said the government is making every effort to promote sports as it is an important part of nation-building under the ‘Viksit Bharat 2047’ initiative. She said the government has launched Yuva Connect to enable sports to go hand in hand with education, with various programmes aimed at promoting sports being conducted in educational institutions.The Union Minister said Mizoram is doing well in various sports disciplines and praised the state’s efforts to identify and nurture young talent. She said she would make every effort to promote development across different sports disciplines.Khadse said young people are the vision of the nation and that the government gives them priority. She said Prime Minister Narendra Modi has been taking steps to promote sports in India since 2014, with various developments taking place under the Khelo India programme.She said efforts are being made through various initiatives to produce more successful athletes, including identifying talented children in cities as well as remote areas, and that many have already benefited from such programmes. She said women’s sporting talent is also being promoted, but much more remains to be done. Stressing the importance of a systematic approach to sports, she said the government is making every effort to provide athletes with greater strength and support, including through proper nutrition, and to build the infrastructure needed for the overall development of sports.

. In Men’s Cricket, India crushed Afghanistan by 127 runs in the third T20I to complete a 3-nil series sweep in New Delhi last night. Put in to bat, India posted 221 runs for the loss of seven wickets in stipulated 20 overs. In reply, Afghanistan were bowled out for 94 in 14.1 overs. Earlier, Afghanistan won the toss and opted to bowl.

. The United Nations Secretary-General António Guterres urged global competitors in artificial intelligence to cooperate in addressing threats from the technology. He warned that the world cannot afford a race to the bottom on AI safety. The Secretary-General told reporters that governments must assume their first responsibility to protect civilians from AI threats- meaning national action is essential, though global coordination is also indispensable.UN Chief was referring to a proposal from Dario Amodei, CEO of Anthropic, to ensure AI safety by coordinating a slowdown in its development by leading technology companies and governments. OpenAI’s Sam Altman, SpaceXAI’s Elon Musk, and other prominent industry leaders have said in recent days that AI’s development needs to slow down. However, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg distanced his company from the stance, saying every AI company has to ensure its technology is safe.

. Union Minister for Electronics and Information Technology Ashwini Vaishnaw today said that SEMICON 2.0 is expected to generate around one lakh crore rupees investment into the semiconductor industry in the coming times. Addressing the media at SEMICON India 2026 in New Delhi, Mr Vaishnaw said that India’s design capability is known across the world. He said that the approach under SEMICON 2.0 will be to promote semiconductor design companies. He noted that the SEMICON 2.0 is also expected to generate up to one lakh employment opportunities.Highlighting the second pillar of SEMICON 2.0 – Machines and Materials, the Minister said that many machine makers and capital equipment makers are participating in the event and are looking to set up their bases in India. He said that those engaged in manufacturing will have the opportunity to connect with the precision manufacturing ecosystem developing in the country.Mr Vaishnaw also informed that under SEMICON 1.0, around four hundred universities and institutes are already teaching chip design to their students. He said the government is now looking forward to upgrading these courses and enabling students to undertake systems design after learning chip design. He said the government is looking forward to scale the technical training by partnering with industries and institutes such as the Industrial Technology Research Institute of Taiwan. He said these institutions can help set up facilities that can train technicians.

. Death toll due to devastating flash floods in Nepal surged to 1410, with over 6100 people still missing. This was stated by the Nepal’s disaster management authority today. According to the data issued by Nepal’s National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority, 364 bodies have been recovered from Chitwan district, 232 from Nawalparasi East, 222 from Nawalparasi West, and 203 from Nuwakot. Similarly, 199 bodies have been recovered from Rasuwa, 78 bodies from Gorkha, 72 bodies from Dhading and 38 bodies from Tanahu. Two flood victims died in Kathmandu hospitals while undergoing treatment. 13,756 people have been rescued from the flood-affected areas so far. The joint command of security personnel continues to carry out search and rescue operations in the flood-affected areas.

. External Affairs Minister Dr. S Jaishankar has said that India stands firmly committed to Bhutan’s progress and prosperity. He joined Bhutan Prime Minister Tshering Tobgay and Foreign Minister DN Dhungyel in launching second phase of international UPI for Bhutanese citizens visiting India.Dr Jaishankar is on a two day visit to Thimpu, Bhutan. In a social media post, he said that together with the use of UPI in Bhutan, this completes two-way UPI-based digital payment connectivity between India and Bhutan. They also witnessed exchange of MoU on extending the Nehru Wangchuck Scholarship Scheme for higher education by Bhutanese students at Indian institutions. Dr Jaishankar termed this a step forward for India-Bhutan cooperation in education and capacity building.The External Affairs Minister also handed over 54 Made in India electric vehicles to Prime Minister Tobgay. The Minister said India is supporting Bhutan’s advances towards e-mobility and sustainability transport. Earlier, Dr Jaishankar called on the Bhutan Prime Minister, saying that he deeply values Mr Tobgay’s sentiments for India-Bhutan unique ties of friendship and cooperation.Yesterday, Dr. Jaishankar received a warm welcome from his Bhutanese counterpart D N Dhungyel on his arrival in the valley town of Paro. The talks between the two ministers focused on advancing multifaceted engagement in development partnership, energy, trade, connectivity, culture and people-to-people ties. He also inaugurated a couple of projects, including a 65-bed Gyaltsuen Jetsun Pema Mother and Child Hospital in Mongar. He also laid the foundation stone for the 500 KW Lunana Hydropower Project in Gasa, northern Bhutan.

. India produced a commanding all-round performance to defeat Sri Lanka by 72 runs in the Women’s Asia Cup 2026 final in Dubai last night, securing a record-extending eighth Asia Cup title. The victory also helped India avenge their defeat to Sri Lanka in the 2024 final. It was India’s sixth win over Sri Lanka in an Asia Cup final across the ODI and T20 formats, including the 2004 edition when India defeated Sri Lanka 5-0 in the two-team tournament.India first posted a formidable 183 for 5 after openers Shafali Verma and Smriti Mandhana produced a record-breaking 129-run partnership. The bowlers then completed the job by dismissing Sri Lanka for 111 in 19.4 overs, with Shree Charani taking four wickets and Deepti Sharma claiming three. Shafali Verma was declared Player of the Match.India’s victory was built on a combination of explosive batting at the top and disciplined bowling through the middle and final overs. The record partnership between Shafali and Mandhana gave India the platform, while Charani and Deepti dismantled Sri Lanka’s chase to seal a memorable eighth title.President Droupadi Murmu, Vice President C P Radhakrishnan and Prime Minister Narendra Modi congratulated all the members of Team India on winning Women’s T20 Asia Cup Championship 2026. In a social media post, the President said that the players played superbly as a team throughout the tournament, winning all the matches and making the country proud. She said that these players are a source of great inspiration for the youth of the country. She also expressed confidence that the team will script many more inspiring chapters of success and excellence.Vice President C P Radhakrishnan also congratulated the team on lifting the Women’s T20 Asia Cup for a record eighth time. He said that the team’s unbeaten campaign, exceptional teamwork and unwavering determination throughout the tournament have brought immense pride to the nation. He also wished the players well for their future endeavours.Prime Minister Modi said that the confidence, consistency and remarkable spirit of the players were on full display throughout the tournament. Congratulating the Women’s team, Mr Modi wished that this triumph inspire millions of youngsters across the country to play more and shine.Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla has congratulated the Indian women’s cricket team via a social media post. Mr Birla lauded the team for remaining unbeaten throughout the tournament and securing victory in the Asia Cup for the 8th time. He added that the cricketers gave a splendid demonstration of their talent and determination in the tournament and this victory is a triumph of the strength, hard work, and dreams of the daughters of India. The Lok Sabha Speaker emphasised that the accomplishment inspires the youth of the country, to dream big, work hard, and move forward with full determination to achieve their goals.

. The Country’s overall workforce participation rate (WPR) for age 15 years and above increased to 52.8 per cent in August, the highest level recorded since March, 2026. According to the monthly labour force and unemployment data released by the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation, rural WPR increased by 1.3 per cent to 55.8 per cent, whereas the urban WPR declined half a per cent to stood at 47 per cent in August.The country’s unemployment rate for persons aged 15 years and above declined marginally to five per cent in August, compared with 5.1 per cent in July this year. According to the monthly labour force and unemployment data released by the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation, the rural unemployment rate eased to 4.1 per cent in August, which is the lowest level since January this year. In contrast, the urban unemployment rate increased slightly to 6.8 per cent, marking a four-month high. Among females, the overall unemployment rate declined to 5.1 per cent, while the unemployment rate among males eased to 4.9 per cent in August.The overall Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR) for age 15 years and above increased moderately to 55.6 per cent in August.

. The 26th Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Summit in Bishkek has concluded with 13 key outcomes. The outcomes cover counter-terrorism, climate action, energy, disaster management and digital cooperation.The summit adopted the historic Bishkek Declaration, marking the SCO’s 25th anniversary. It also approved four MoUs and more than 20 decisions.A major decision was to include English as an official SCO language. Leaders also agreed to establish a Universal Centre for Countering Security Threats.The measures will strengthen cooperation against terrorism, extremism, organised crime and other transnational threats. They will also improve security information sharing.Several decisions focus on tackling drug trafficking and synthetic drugs. These include stronger coordination among law enforcement agencies and a cooperation programme on combating drug addiction until 2030. The measures support India’s efforts against cross-border narcotics trafficking and narco-terrorism.On climate and energy, SCO members agreed to enhance cooperation on energy conservation and efficiency. They also adopted a memorandum on combating climate change. These measures support India’s energy security and climate-resilient development goals.The summit also adopted a statement on assistance to countries affected by emergencies. It will strengthen cooperation in disaster management and humanitarian assistance, an area where India has significant capabilities.In the digital sector, members agreed to expand cooperation in artificial intelligence. The move will provide India an opportunity to share its digital and AI expertise and promote responsible and inclusive use of the technology.An agreement on information cooperation will also promote institutional exchanges and help strengthen India’s engagement with the regional media space.The Ministry of External Affairs said the outcomes give India a strategic platform to advance its positions on regional security, development and connectivity. They also strengthen India’s engagement with Central Asia and the wider Eurasian region.The MEA said, addressing the summit, Prime Minister Narendra Modi called for a roadmap for the next 25 years. He stressed the need for concrete outcomes in the areas of security, connectivity and opportunity.The two-day SCO Summit was held at Bishkek in Kyrgyzstan, from August 31 to September 1.

. United Nations Secretary-General António Guterres has said that global powers that themselves violate international law sit in the Security Council. He stressed on reform of the 15-nation global body saying that it must be an absolute priority. He also underscored the need for redistribution of power.Mr. Guterres said that it is unacceptable to have a Security Council with a composition that reflects the world of many decades ago instead of reflecting today’s world. He said this while addressing a press conference at the world headquarters ahead of the opening of the high-level week of the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly.On the BRICS grouping, Mr. Guterres said that the world is changing, and it is witnessing the emergence of new powers. He said, one thing that is essential in this redistribution of power is the reform of multilateral institutions.
